case_number: Criminal Appeal No(s). OF 2022 (Arising out of Special Leave Petition (Crl.) No.2420 of 2022)
summary: The appeals challenged the Manipur High Court's decision to set aside an order of preventive detention under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1988. The High Court held that illegible and blurred copies of documents relied upon in the detention order were supplied, undermining the detenu's right under Article 22(5) of the Constitution to make an effective representation. The State argued the issue was not raised before the detaining authority, but the Supreme Court emphasized that non-supply of legible documents constitutes a violation of a fundamental right, irrespective of prior objection. The Supreme Court upheld the High Court's judgment, affirming that denial of clear documents vitiated the detention process.
legal_provisions_cited: Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1988
Smt. Dharmista Bhagat v. State of Karnataka & Another, 1989 Supp (2) SCC 155
Manjit Singh Grewal @ Gogi v. Union of India & Ors., 1990 (Supp.) SCC 59
Mehrunissa v. State of Maharashtra, (1981) 2 SCC 709
Bhupinder Singh v. Union of India & Others, (1987) 2 SCC 234
Ramchandra A. Kamat v. Union of India and Others, (1980) 2 SCC 270
final_judgment: Appeal dismissed; the High Court's order quashing the detention was upheld as the failure to supply legible documents violated Article 22(5) of the Constitution.
